name: the Samaritan
note: Traveler in the parable who tends a robbery victim (ch. 10).

name: Wounded traveler in the Samaritan parable
note: Unnamed man inside the story Jesus tells in Luke 10:30–35, traveling from Jerusalem to Jericho, stripped, beaten and left half dead. Distinct from the framing lawyer and from the Samaritan who helps him. Injuries and lost clothing are situational, not a separate life stage.

name: Robbers in the Samaritan parable
note: Unnamed group inside Jesus’s story in Luke 10:30 who attack the traveler and depart. Distinct from the men crucified with Jesus and all other robbery groups. Describe a typical member.

name: Priest in the Samaritan parable
note: Unnamed priest inside the narrated story in Luke 10:31, who sees the traveler and passes on the other side. Distinct from every named priest elsewhere and from the framing speakers.

name: Levite in the Samaritan parable
note: Unnamed Levite inside the narrated story in Luke 10:32, who sees the traveler and passes on the other side. Distinct from the priest immediately before him and from named Levites elsewhere.

name: Innkeeper in the Samaritan parable
note: Unnamed host of the inn inside the story in Luke 10:35, entrusted with the injured traveler’s care and given two denarii. Distinct from the Samaritan, injured traveler and framing speakers.

name: Samaritan’s mount in the parable
note: The Samaritan’s own animal inside the story in Luke 10:34, used to carry the injured man to the inn. The text fixes ownership and use but not species, colour or markings; any chosen species/appearance is illustrative invention or tradition, not a textual claim.

name: Jerusalem–Jericho road in the Samaritan parable
note: The descending journey from Jerusalem to Jericho inside the narrated story in Luke 10:30–34. It is the inner story’s road, not the location of Jesus’s conversation with the lawyer. The text fixes endpoints and descending travel; specific terrain details follow the era/illustrative tradition.

name: Inn in the Samaritan parable
note: Unnamed inn inside the narrated story in Luke 10:34–35, where the Samaritan brings the injured traveler and pays the host. Distinct from the road and from the framing conversation. The text gives an inn, not a specific architectural description.
